findings.title: Distinct base events can still share one transaction ordinal

evidence.detail: First-event order is nondecreasing. Equal ordinals are accepted when frame and before_* prefixes match, without requiring the two tags to describe the same actual READ transaction.
New controls check missing/duplicate events, out-of-order rows and individual bounds, but not distinct base events sharing one otherwise coherent ordinal/prefix.

findings.source_derived_counterexample: In the generated healthy BASE_P control, first RESET has ordinal1/frame1/all-zero prefix. First GROUP has ordinal2/frame1/before_reset1 and other prefix counts0. Editing only the GROUP relationship tuple to ordinal1/before_reset0 makes it share the RESET prefix. Other rows, all counts and the PASS verdict stay unchanged. Current validation accepts it: equal-prefix equality is permitted, GROUP is still before SET/READ/second GROUP, and all bounds hold. One question cannot simultaneously be GROUP and RESET. A SET-refusal case can still unlock at its unaffected real trajectory using this damaged positive. No test/probe was run by reviewer.
minimum_fix: Require distinct base events to have strictly increasing ordinals. Permit an equal ordinal only for the legitimate ordered first READ followed by read_consumable tag of that same READ, with identical frame and complete prefix. This is a bounded existing-schema check, not a full history reconstruction or new report framework.

Add a positive-first damaged GROUP/RESET equal-ordinal relationship control that rejects before output/preparation/boot/provider/effect for the ordinal relationship. Keep the valid same-READ read/read_consumable positive and the legitimate group/set/reset-only control. Retain genuine parent RED and corrected focused GREEN.

findings.title: Terrain and environment callbacks bypass the continuation latch

evidence.detail: note_callback is called by model and settling wrappers, but boot_config passes the functions returned by host.terrain_provider and host.env_provider directly to Engine. Those provider invocations are not recorded as continuation.

The public boot contract takes actual terrain and environment Lua functions; these are genuine host callback surfaces, not setup-only values. The environment function is also the default sound metadata/backend provider.
The new continued-fault control only calls config.bind_mobile before rethrowing the same marker. It never exercises config.terrain or config.environment.

findings.source_derived_counterexample: After ignoring an injected fault, a scripted campaign can invoke config.terrain or config.environment and then raise the original expected marker in the same engine entry. r.callback stays nil and the new fatal.entry join matches r.entry, so the refusal still receives PASS even though another host callback continued past the bad answer. No experiment was replayed.
minimum_fix: Transparently wrap both actual returned provider callables through the same continuation tracking, forwarding every argument and every result exactly once without adding physical/provider queries or changing their errors, state or order. Cover the real callback functions rather than merely the provider factories.

Use the genuine direct-refusal positive first, then ignored-fault->terrain callback->same-marker and ignored-fault->environment callback->same-marker negatives during both relevant boot/frame entries. They must fail for continued callback; preserve direct immediate refusal, normal-return failure, other-marker failure and valid changed-answer cases. No native damaged-input run or C/Rust/build change is needed.
findings.prior_subcases_closed_at_source: The new pending refusal latch, model/named-callback continuation checks, normal-return stop, actual boot/frame fatal capture and same-entry comparison close the originally demonstrated bind_mobile/delayed-frame cases. Missing two callback surfaces prevents closure of the SAME original finding.
